title: After Midnight
content:
Lila had imagined many versions of her first night with Darius.

In some, she was effortlessly confident. In others, she said something embarrassing and spent the next decade remembering it at three in the morning.

The reality was more complicated.

They stood in her living room, kissing between quiet laughter and whispered conversations, discovering that the attraction which had started in the afternoon sunshine had only deepened.

Darius never rushed her.

When she pulled away to catch her breath, he waited. When she laughed at her own nervousness, he laughed with her instead of making her feel foolish.

It was that patience, more than his confidence, that finally allowed her to relax.

“You're very quiet,” he murmured.

“I'm deciding whether I like you.”

“And?”

“Still under review.”

He smiled.

“That's fair.”

She touched his cheek.

“Do you always make it this difficult to dislike you?”

“Only when the woman is worth the effort.”

Lila kissed him before he could say anything else.

For a while, the world outside her house became irrelevant. The rain tapped against the windows, the lights cast a warm glow over the room, and every conversation seemed to lead them back to one another.

Eventually, Darius rested his forehead against hers.

“Lila, I don't want you to feel like you have to do anything because you've invited me in.”

She looked into his eyes.

“I know.”

“I'm serious.”

“So am I.” She took his hand. “I'm here because I want to be here.”

His expression softened.

“Then I'm exactly where I want to be.”

She led him toward the hallway, stopping at her bedroom door.

For the first time that evening, she felt a flutter of uncertainty.

Darius noticed.

“What's going through that head of yours?”

“I'm wondering whether tomorrow morning is going to be awkward.”

He considered the question.

“I can promise to make you coffee.”

“You don't know how I take it?”

“Black. No sugar.”

She laughed.

“You remembered.”

“I remember a lot about you.”

She looked at him, her teasing expression giving way to something more vulnerable.

“That's what scares me.”

“Why?”

“Because I might actually start liking you.”

Darius stepped closer but left the decision to her.

“Lila, I think we've passed that point.”

She smiled, then drew him into another kiss.

The bedroom door closed behind them.

What followed belonged to them alone: whispered reassurances, laughter when nerves interrupted the moment, and the slow discovery of a closeness that neither wanted to rush. There was no performance, no expectation that either of them had to be perfect. Only two adults choosing to trust one another.

Much later, when the rain had stopped and the room had fallen quiet, Lila rested against Darius, listening to the steady rhythm of his breathing.

She had expected attraction.

She hadn't expected comfort.

“Are you awake?” she whispered.

“Unfortunately.”

She laughed against his shoulder.

“Rude.”

“You woke me up to insult me.”

“I have questions.”

“Of course you do.”

She lifted her head.

“Why did you really leave the city?”

His smile disappeared.

For a moment, she thought he would avoid the question. Instead, he stared toward the darkened window.

“My engagement ended.”

Lila went still.

“Engagement?”

“Six months ago.”

She sat up slightly.

“You were engaged?”

“Yes.”

“And you didn't think that was worth mentioning over dinner?”

“I wasn't hiding it. I just didn't want our first date to become a conversation about my past.”

Lila understood that, at least in theory. But the discovery still unsettled her.

“Do you still love her?”

“No.”

The answer came quickly, but his expression remained complicated.

“Then what happened?”

Darius exhaled.

“She wanted a life that looked perfect from the outside. I wanted a life that felt right when the doors were closed. We spent too long pretending those were the same thing.”

Lila studied him.

“And now you're here.”

“Now I'm here.”

She wanted to believe that was the end of the story.

But as she settled back against him, another thought crept into her mind.

If Darius had been engaged to someone he once intended to marry, there was a whole part of his life she knew nothing about.

And she was beginning to care enough for that ignorance to hurt.
